reviews.text: Just awful. We had an 8 AM appointment and at 8:45. We still hadn't been seen. I waited another five minutes at the front desk with not one person coming up to help me.

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ **Absolutely five stars. They have earned my trust.**

I am incredibly grateful for Christown Animal Hospital and the care they have given my animals. After two very different situations with two of my pets, I can confidently say this is a veterinary practice I trust and will continue using.

My nine-year-old dog, Khaleesi, needed to be spayed, and because of her age I was understandably nervous about putting her through surgery. She also had a mass that needed to be removed, and they were able to take care of both procedures at the same time. She came through surgery beautifully and recovered extremely well. I couldn't have asked for a better outcome.

Then there was my Burmese cat, Chubbins.

Before bringing her to Christown, I took her to a veterinary dental specialist because I knew she had dental problems. I left that appointment absolutely devastated after being told that Chubbins needed a **full-mouth extraction—every single tooth in her mouth removed**.

I decided to get another opinion and brought her to Christown.

They performed her dental cleaning, carefully evaluated her teeth, and in the end **only four teeth needed to be extracted**. FOUR. Not her entire mouth.

Chubbins came through the procedure wonderfully, and I cannot express how relieved and grateful I am that I sought another opinion before agreeing to such a drastic procedure.

What I appreciate most about Christown is that I feel like my animals are being treated as individuals. I want a veterinarian who looks at the animal in front of them, determines what actually needs to be done, and doesn't automatically jump to the most aggressive or extreme treatment.

Between successfully spaying my nine-year-old dog and removing her mass at the same time, and then taking such good care of Chubbins and preserving almost all of her teeth, **Christown Animal Hospital has absolutely earned my confidence and my business.**

Finding a veterinarian you genuinely trust with animals you love is incredibly important. I've found that here.

**I will absolutely be bringing my animals back in the future. Five stars and highly recommended.**

Pull it out and the Doc walks back in and I show them and they shrug and go "ok. $80 for the visit". I bring up that I have united pet care "pet insurance" and nobody at the front desk seems to know what it is or be able to apply the discount.

If I could give this less than a one star I would.  I would like to say first off the first time I visited this vet clinic I had a good experience. I nice woman took care of my dog and the vet tech was very pleasant. This is the reason I went again when one of my other dogs was having urinary issues.  First off, I walked in the door and urine was all over the lobby and no one was cleaning it up. We were the only ones in the waiting room so I picked up some paper towels and started to clean it up myself because I didn't want my dog walking through other dogs urine.  The reception person didn't even acknowledge that I was doing anything or said anything when I pointed out the urine.  Then we were taken back to a room. There were no smiles nor greetings for my dog. The exam room was dirty, I had to wipe off the chairs before I sat down and the floor was not clean. The vet came in and was less than friendly and ask some questions, felt of my dogs belly then ordered x-rays and blood work.  They did not do a  urine analysis because I suspected a urinary tract infection.  Long story short I feel as though I was swindled out of $700. He showed me her organs in the x-ray that really only shows bones. Her liver enzymes were high but still no urine analysis. He just wanted to prescribe meds "Just in case".  I really should have gotten upset there but I was in a bit of shock with everything that went down. Now upon reflection and talking to my daughter who is a vet tech, I feel like they saw me coming and thought ChaChing $$$..  I will NOT be returning.  You would be wise and richer if you do too.

From the front desk to the vet techs and vet my experience was flawless.  Everyone knew what they were doing and things were done correctly and efficiently.  Can’t say thank you enough as well as appreciate you ALL!

I also had him do the Anal Gland Expression because Mac Keeps scooting his Butt on the Gravel Rocks!!  It has to HURT!!  I couldn’t even imagine what that would feel like!!

Horrible Experience today!
I asked the vet if he could write a prescription for our dogs medicine vs. having their office fill it and charge us. The other two medicines we did pay for to be filled right there. I took the prescription for Clavamox to my regular pharmacy but they couldn't fill it due to the amount of medicine being too small.(normally an adult dose needed would be in a larger amount) They suggested I get it through Chewy.com. but when I called Chewy the vet told me that the Vet that wrote the prescription would have to call it in or it had to be faxed from the Vets office. I figured I might as well just go get the medicine from the Vets clinic after all since it was only a few dollars difference.
I went back to our Vets office to give them back the prescription(we were charged $11 initially for just the Vet having to write the prescription). I explained to them that my pharmacy couldn't fill it and that I would just purchase the med through them. I asked the front desk girl if they could deduct the $11 we had to pay for the prescription to be written from the cost of the medicine and she said she had to ask the Vet. After waiting about 10-15 minutes I told them to just forget it and that I would pay the full price for the medication because my mom was waiting in a hot car outside and we were in a hurry. After the girl handed me the medicine without giving me any instructions, I noticed that I only got 30 mls. of the medicine when the original prescription was for 50 mls..My first thought was that I didn't have enough medicine to give him based on the instructions from the original prescription. I asked the girl why I only got 30 mls and told her that I didn't think it would be enough. She then told me she would call the vet out to talk to me. Dr. Sandhu Gurjit came out and he ghen explained to me that the medicine he wrote for was a higher concentration. I then told him okay and that I understood. Next, I heard him whisper to the front desk lady that I was not to be seen ever again and to note it on the account.
U was completely taken aback and questioned them as to why I could ever come back when all I was asking was for clarification on the dosage. The girl told me that I was yelling and being aggressive. Funny because my tone never got nasty and my voice had never gotten loud and in fact it was the girl that started yelling at me!

I told their office I would be making a report to the Board of Veterinary Medicine because this office makes it a routine to have customers think their pet is being seen by a Veterinarian yet on many occasions my dogs were NOT seen by the Vet but instead were seen by the Vet Tech. Heather. On those occasions when she saw my dogs I was told that she was going to call the Veterinarian on the phone. My dogs also received prescription medicine without being visually seen by a licensed Veterinarian. In other visits with my animals I was told that my pet would be seen by the Vet and that that "Vet" would then call another Vet over the phone to confirm the plan of care. In other words I was lied to for a few years until I finally wised up and asked Heather myself if she was a Veterinarian and she then told me "no" that she was a Vet Tech..
This office runs their clinic without a Veterinarian at the clinic most of the days and is lying to patrons making them think their pet is being seen by a Veterinarian.
Finally, I had brought my barely 1 lb.,6 month old, Chihuahua in for vomiting and diarrhea and this Vet Tech Heather went and shoved a wooden handled, dry, Qtip an inch and a half up my puppies rectum causing her to bleed from her rectum and excruciating pain for days. Sooo dangerous! I had to fight to hold back tears as my puppy screamed in agony.  Think twice about taking any animal to this Flop House of a clinic!
